items.title: Terminator 2: Judgment Day
items.line: Opened in the US on 3 July 1991 and grossed roughly $520 million worldwide. At the time it was the most expensive film ever made.

items.title: The Silence of the Lambs
items.line: Out since February, it swept the Big Five at the 64th Oscars: Picture, Director, Actor, Actress and Adapted Screenplay. It cost $19 million and made about $273 million.

items.title: Nevermind
items.line: Nirvana's album came out on 24 September 1991. US shops got only 46,251 copies at first. By 11 January 1992 it was number one, ahead of Michael Jackson.

items.title: Sonic the Hedgehog
items.line: Sega's answer to Mario hit the Genesis in June 1991. From November it was bundled with US consoles, and it became the best-selling Genesis game at over 15 million copies.

items.title: Super Nintendo
items.line: The SNES reached US shops on 23 August 1991 for $199, with Super Mario World in the box. UK kids had to wait until April 1992 and paid £150.
